translationRepairs: s0003 Chinese 〈（王誌道）〉 is a sub-biography heading; the idiomatic English wrongly retains stray ]〉 markup after Wang Zhidao, so removing those characters restores a clean heading without changing meaning.
s0003’s trailing 〉 is Chinese corner-bracket markup, not part of the parenthetical name; stripping it from the literal line corrects corruption without altering the name.
He was appointed as the investigating censor for Pingyang Prefecture.
He was appointed prefectural judge of Pingyang Prefecture.
s0007 授平陽府推官 names the prefectural judicial post 推官; investigating censor would be 御史/巡按, and s0008’s later 擢御史 confirms this first post was not a censorate office.
He was appointed investigating censor of Pingyang Prefecture.
He was appointed prefectural judge of Pingyang Prefecture.
Literal s0007 likewise mistranslates 推官 as investigating censor; prefectural judge matches the prefecture’s judicial official.

When Grand Coordinator Li Hualong stepped down to observe mourning, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the five eastern Shang routes, and abolish the mining commissioner.

When Governor-General Li Hualong stepped down to observe mourning, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the five eastern routes of Shu, and abolish the mining commissioner.

s0013 總督李化龍 is Governor-General, not Grand Coordinator (巡撫); 上東五路 is not “Shang routes,” and in the Sichuan/Bozhou context the repair’s “five eastern routes of Shu” correctly drops the false Shang reading.

When Grand Coordinator Li Hualong left on account of bereavement, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the five routes of eastern Shang, and abolish the mining commissioner.

When Governor-General Li Hualong left on account of bereavement, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the five eastern routes of Shu, and abolish the mining commissioner.
Literal s0013 has the same errors: 總督 ≠ Grand Coordinator, and 上東五路 is not eastern Shang; Governor-General and five eastern routes of Shu restore the Chinese sense.
Later Yan, Zhen, Jineng, and others used their record of compliance to demand the markets be restored; he ultimately refused, saving more than a hundred thousand taels of gold and silver annually.
Later Jineng of Yanzhen and others used their record of compliance to demand the markets be restored; he ultimately refused, saving more than a hundred thousand taels of gold and silver annually.
s0022 延鎮吉能等 is Jineng of the Yan border garrison (延鎮) and others, not three persons Yan, Zhen, and Jineng; the repair correctly reunites place and tribal leader.
Later Yan, Zhen, Jineng, and others leveraged their good faith to demand restoration of the fairs; he ultimately refused, saving more than a hundred thousand in gold and silver each year.
Later Jineng of Yanzhen and others leveraged their good faith to demand restoration of the fairs; he ultimately refused, saving more than a hundred thousand in gold and silver each year.
Literal 延鎮吉能 likewise means Jineng of Yanzhen, not Yan, Zhen, Jineng as separate names.
He was appointed as the investigating censor for Songjiang.
He was appointed prefectural judge of Songjiang.
s0105 除松江推官 is appointment as prefectural judge (推官), not investigating censor; the following capital justice post does not rewrite this first office.
He was appointed investigating censor of Songjiang.
He was appointed prefectural judge of Songjiang.
Literal s0105 repeats the 推官→investigating censor error; prefectural judge is the accurate office.
When his mourning period ended he was assigned to defend Jining in Ji Prefecture.
When his mourning period ended he was assigned as defense commissioner of the Ji-Ning Circuit.
s0108 分守冀寧 assigns him as defense commissioner of the Ji-Ning Circuit; “Jining in Ji Prefecture” mis-parses 冀寧 as a county-in-prefecture place-name.
When his period of mourning ended he was assigned to defend Jining in Ji Prefecture.
When his period of mourning ended he was assigned as defense commissioner of the Ji-Ning Circuit.
Literal s0108 has the same misreading of 冀寧; defense commissioner of the Ji-Ning Circuit matches 分守 plus the circuit name.
In the winter of the first year of Tianqi he was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
In the winter of the first year of Tianqi he was granted the additional honor of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
s0082 加太子太保 marks an added honorific (加), not a territorial enfeoffment (封); “granted the additional honor of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent” matches the Chinese.
In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi Liaoyang fell.
In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang fell.
Chinese 天啟元年四月，遼陽覆 separates the date from the event; without the comma, English can fuse “Tianqi Liaoyang,” so inserting the comma restores the source punctuation’s sense.
In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi Liaoyang fell.
In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi, Liaoyang fell.
Literal s0113 needs the same date/event comma to match Chinese 天啟元年四月，遼陽覆.

Earlier, on completion of his term review he was enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; citing the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping, he was further promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

Earlier, on completion of his term review he was granted the honor of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; citing the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping, he was further promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

s0165 加太子少保…再進太子太保 correctly marks honorific advancement (加), not enfeoffment, but 保 is Guardian (as in s0082 太子太保), not Tutor (傅); the proposal still keeps Tutor, so the field is revised to Junior/Grand Guardian.

Earlier, on completion of his term review he was enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; recounting the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping, he was further promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

Earlier, on completion of his term review he was granted the honor of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; recounting the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping, he was further promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
Literal s0165 likewise needs 加→granted honor and 保→Guardian rather than Tutor; the proposal only fixed enfeoffment.
The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Grand Canal granary.
The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Taicang treasury.
s0175 貯太倉 refers to the Ministry of Revenue’s Taicang treasury/storehouse, not a Grand Canal granary; the repair matches the fiscal institution named in the Chinese.
The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Grand Canal granary.
The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Taicang treasury.
Literal s0175 has the same 太倉 misreading; Taicang treasury is correct.

In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to supervise Liaodong supplies from Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed.

In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, to supervise Liaodong supplies from Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed.
s0193 右僉都御史 is Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief (僉都御史); Vice Censor-in-Chief would be 副都御史, so the repair restores the correct censorate rank.

In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong supplies, stationed at Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed to it.

In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong supplies, stationed at Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed to it.
Literal s0193 likewise mislabels 僉都御史 as Vice; Assistant Censor-in-Chief is accurate.
What enters the inner palace exceeds six million; what enters the Grand Canal granary, apart from goods-in-kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.
What enters the inner palace exceeds six million; what enters the Taicang treasury, apart from goods-in-kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.
s0196 入太倉者 again names the Taicang treasury opposite 內府, not the Grand Canal granary.
What enters the inner palace exceeds six million; what enters the Grand Canal granary, apart from goods-in-kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.
What enters the inner palace exceeds six million; what enters the Taicang treasury, apart from goods-in-kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.
Literal s0196 requires the same 太倉→Taicang treasury correction.

The Collected Statutes concerning the Grand Canal granary state: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that capital transport grain and funds from all places, whether golden-flower grain or not, that should have gone to the inner palace were all to be stored in the Grand Canal granary for use on the borders.

The Collected Statutes concerning the Taicang treasury state: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that capital transport grain and funds from all places, whether golden-flower grain or not, that should have gone to the inner palace were all to be stored in the Taicang treasury storehouse for use on the borders.
s0206 《會典》於太倉庫…悉解貯太倉庫 names the Taicang treasury storehouse twice; Grand Canal granary is a false gloss of 太倉.

The Collected Statutes concerning the Grand Canal granary state: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that grain and funds transported to the capital from all places, whether golden-flower grain or not, that should have gone to the inner palace were all to be stored in the Grand Canal granary for use on the borders.

The Collected Statutes concerning the Taicang treasury state: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that grain and funds transported to the capital from all places, whether golden-flower grain or not, that should have gone to the inner palace were all to be stored in the Taicang treasury storehouse for use on the borders.
Literal s0206 has the same 太倉庫 misreading; Taicang treasury / storehouse is correct.
whether future funds should aid the borders or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Grand Canal granary—that too may be done.
whether future funds should aid the borders or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Taicang treasury—that too may be done.
s0212 盡還太倉 means return funds to the Taicang treasury, not a Grand Canal granary.
whether future funds should aid the borders or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Grand Canal granary—that too may be done.
whether future funds should aid the borders or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Taicang treasury—that too may be done.
Literal s0212 likewise requires Taicang treasury for 太倉.
Offending Wei Zhongxian, he received an edict of stern rebuke; the court ministers were again announced to that anyone who memorialized again would be punished without pardon.
Offending Wei Zhongxian, he received an edict of stern rebuke; the court ministers were again told that anyone who memorialized again would be punished without pardon.

s0233 復宣諭廷臣 means the court ministers were again instructed/told; “were again announced to that” is ungrammatical and misrenders 宣諭, while the proposed wording matches the idiomatic line and the Chinese.
The emperor was angry, reduced Shu's rank by inscription, and transferred him outside the capital.
The emperor was angry, demoted Shu, and transferred him outside the capital.
s0254 鐫樞級 means Ge Shu was demoted in grade; “reduced … rank by inscription” is an unnatural calque of 鐫, and “demoted Shu” is accurate, complete English for the penalty.
Xue Zhen died at the hands of the eunuch faction.
Xue Zhen was put to death as a member of the eunuch faction.
s0258 以奄黨抵死 means he was condemned to death as a eunuch-faction associate, not that the faction killed him; aligning the literal with the correct idiomatic reading removes the inverted agent.
